transit.title: Restore Safe, Accessible Local Transit Along Finch West
transit.searchDescription: Line 6 replaced the 36 Finch West local bus, so many riders walk farther. Lorna Antwi's plan to bring back local buses on Finch West, all day, before winter.

stakeholders.paragraph: TTC riders; people with disabilities, injuries, chronic illnesses or limited mobility; seniors; Toronto Community Housing residents; shift workers; students; local businesses; residents of Wards 1, 6 and 7.

items.item: Restore convenient local transit access throughout the day.
Reduce unnecessary walking distances and transfers.
Preserve independent access to healthcare, employment, shopping and community services.
Account for different mobility limitations, walking speeds, rest requirements and winter conditions.
Restore access to nighttime Request Stop protections where local bus service is reinstated.
Reduce unsafe walks and transfers after dark.
Identify unsafe pedestrian connections, inadequate lighting and weather exposure.
Reduce missed connections and unnecessary travel time.
Improve connections between neighbourhoods, workplaces, medical facilities and the LRT.
Measure complete journeys, not just vehicle travel speeds.
Publish the calculations and assumptions used to justify removing local service.
Compare projected benefits against residents' actual experiences.
Identify who gained and who lost access.
Require documented TTC decisions addressing accessibility and safety concerns.

proposedAction.paragraph: Once signing closes on October 26, 2026, I will submit a community petition requesting that the TTC assess disability-related barriers and provide effective accommodation through restoration of the former 36 Finch West local bus service, or equivalent neighbourhood coverage, alongside Line 6.
Service must operate throughout the day, including midday, evenings and early mornings, restoring convenient local stops and nighttime Request Stop protections.

We request urgent restoration before winter. If the TTC proposes an alternative accommodation, we request a written explanation of how it addresses the identified barriers. Should the TTC refuse accommodation on grounds of undue hardship, we request a written decision identifying the specific evidence, financial figures and legal grounds supporting that refusal.

group.title: Public Consultation & Decision-Making
group.item: 2022: Of the 100 people who answered the TTC consultation question, 81% identified destinations they expected to lose access to between LRT stops previously served by the 36 Finch West bus. The question concerned proposed Emery Village changes involving replacement of the 36D/F branches.
2022: Respondents requested full-day and overnight alternatives, rather than service limited to conventional working hours.
November 2023: TTC planners acknowledged that removing local stops would require longer walks while describing network-wide walking-time impacts as minimal.
November 22, 2023: The TTC Board approved the 2024 Annual Service Plan, including bus route removals and replacements.
December 2025: The 36C Finch West service was eliminated following the opening of Line 6.

group.title: Walking Distances & Accessibility
group.item: TTC Service Standards: 400 metres in 5 minutes for regular service; 1,250 metres in 15 minutes overnight.
TTC accessibility guidance states that walking distances are calculated using 1 metre per second to accommodate slower pedestrians.
Toronto's Complete Streets Guidelines warn that typical walking-speed assumptions can exclude one-third of older pedestrians and 90% of pedestrians using mobility aids.
City guideline recommendation: Walking speeds for certain pedestrian crossings "should be in the range of 0.8m/s to 1.0m/s".

paragraph.strong: Comparison of TTC stated walking times against slower walking speeds:
The overnight distance takes approximately 11 minutes longer at 0.8 m/s than the TTC's stated 15 minutes.

group.paragraph: These calculations exclude additional delays from rest breaks, pain, inaccessible crossings, snow and ice.
The TTC's coverage standards are network-wide planning targets. The published standards do not establish which walking speeds were applied to individual journeys in the Finch West restructuring.

group.title: Travel-Time Modelling
group.item: The TTC's service-planning methodology compares projected travel-time improvements against disadvantages across affected passenger groups.
A network-wide improvement does not establish that individual riders, particularly those with disabilities, retained safe and practical access.
The route-specific calculations have not been obtained to establish whether disability-related walking speeds, winter conditions and individual safety impacts were separately assessed.

group.title: Nighttime Safety
group.item: The TTC's Request Stop Program allows passengers travelling alone on buses between 9 p.m. and 5 a.m. to request safe drop-offs between regular stops.
This protection is available on buses, not LRT vehicles.
The 336 Finch West overnight bus remains operational, but the LRT replaced local bus service during regular operating hours.
Residents using the LRT after 9 p.m. cannot request the same between-stop drop-off that the former local bus provided.

group.title: Winter Conditions & Sidewalk Accessibility
group.item: Winter 2025-26: Toronto Pearson recorded 160.2 cm of snowfall between December and February, its highest recorded winter total.
January 28, 2026: Toronto's City Manager acknowledged failures in sidewalk snow clearing following widespread complaints.
2025-26: Toronto recorded 14,403 sidewalk snow-clearing requests and 3,020 icy-sidewalk requests.
Toronto's Complete Streets Guidelines identify snow removal, safe pedestrian connections and accessible transit stops as street-design considerations.

group.title: Disability & Independent Living
group.item: 54% of Toronto Community Housing households report having at least one member with a disability.
TTC Community Bus standards recognize slower walking speeds and establish a 175-metre access-distance target for eligible community-bus service.
Wheel-Trans eligibility and advance scheduling mean it cannot simply replace the flexibility of conventional local transit for every disabled rider.

group.title: Existing Accessibility Requirements
group.item: Ontario Regulation 191/11, Section 41, requires transit providers to manage, evaluate and act on accessibility feedback and hold at least one annual public meeting involving people with disabilities.
The TTC's 2025 Annual Public Forum on Accessible Transit occurred October 20, before Line 6 opened.
The next accessibility forum is scheduled for November 10, 2026.
The TTC's next scheduled Board meeting is December 15, 2026.

tools.label: Tools: Established Policy and Regulation
tools.paragraph: USE - TTC Service Standards, Sections 2.3, 2.4 and 5.1: Request urgent consideration of all-day local bus restoration using existing service-review procedures, walking-distance standards and accessibility considerations.

USE - Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act, Ontario Regulation 191/11, Section 41: Submit documented accessibility barriers through the TTC's required feedback process and request consideration before the November 10 accessibility forum.

SUPPORT WITH - Ontario Human Rights Commission Policy on Disability Accommodation and Undue Hardship: Present the restoration request as a disability accommodation issue. If accommodation is refused on undue-hardship grounds, request a written explanation supported by objective evidence concerning costs, available outside funding, and health and safety.

SUPPORT WITH - City of Toronto Complete Streets Guidelines, Chapter 9: Demonstrate the need to consider slower walking speeds, safe pedestrian access and winter maintenance when assessing transit accessibility.

USE - TTC Board Procedures By-law, Section 18 - Public Petitions: Submit the community petition requesting immediate consideration of restoration before winter, to a Board member under Section 18 if the issue is not on the agenda. Request a documented response and ask the member to introduce the petition for Board consideration if the issue remains unresolved.

commitment.heading: Lorna's Commitment to Ward 7
commitment.paragraph: There's no time to waste. Winter is coming, and the annual TTC disability consultation meeting is November 10th.

Signing closes on October 26th, and I intend to present this petition to the TTC Board right after, allowing enough time for word to spread and for the first meeting of the newly appointed TTC Board, on December 15th, to explicitly address the request.
Were I in office, I'd have more power to address this. But the first Council meeting after the election doesn't happen until after November 10th, and there's no time to waste.
We're stronger together, and I don't have to be in office for us to deliver on this promise: that I will make an effort to achieve meaningful, measurable change.

section.heading: Support the Petition: Restore Safe Local Transit Along Finch West Before Winter
section.paragraph: Support the community petition requesting urgent restoration of accessible local bus service throughout the day.
Residents can support the petition without disclosing a disability or providing personal medical information.

trustDisclosure.paragraph: The Finch West LRT provides rapid transit service, and the 336 overnight bus remains operational. This proposal addresses local access lost through the replacement of former bus routes.

The TTC's original corridor-specific calculations and restoration costs have not yet been independently verified. Permanent restoration may require TTC Board approval and additional operating funding.
